This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19
and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer's Order (September
22, 2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the vote will
be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may observe
the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be live
streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting .

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to submit
email correspondence to bsaJeaumua@ malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before the item you
would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency,
as well as states of emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, state of
California, and a federal emergency declared by the President of the United States. In order to
reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the City Council meeting will be open and public but
conducted virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health or safety
of attendees. This way the public, the staff, and the Council will not be physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items, which are
not listed on the agenda but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action
may be taken, the Commission and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing
response. Each speaker is limited to (3) three minutes. Members of the public wishing to speak during the
meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before
the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom
conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions
for signing up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous
meeting where the public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not
subject to public discussion at this meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final.
Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the
decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If
discussion is desired, an item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration.
Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to
the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar
will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent Calendar. The Commission first
will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public speakers shall follow
the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this
meeting with no final action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under
Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment
shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above
are on file in the office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing
bsaleaumua@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for
the deaf (TDD), please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In

Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Peak called the meeting to order at 5:33 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance via teleconference by the Recording
  Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Alicia Peak; Vice Chair Dane Skophammer; and Commissioners
  Georgia Goldfarb (arrived at 5:35 p.m.), Suzanne Guldimann, and Cayley Jenner

  ALSO PRESENT: Jesse Bobbett, Community Services Director; Kristin Riesgo,
  Community Services Deputy Director; Kate Gallo, Recreation Manager; and Brittany
  Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

  At 5:35 p.m., Commissioner Goldfarb joined the meeting.

ITEM4  OLD BUSINESS

  A.  Malibu Bluffs Park Snack Shack
  Recommended Action: Receive an update and provide feedback to staff regarding
  the Snack Shack at Malibu Bluffs Park.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of October I 8, 2022
  Page 3 of 6

Jake Lingo stated he was disappointed the Snack Shack project could not move
forward as previously approved by the Commission. He stated staff should continue
exploring options for a functional Snack Shack at Malibu Bluffs Park that would
allow local youth sports organizations to sell food and refreshments. He stated food
trucks did not generate enough revenue to support local youth sports organizations.

Robert Gold asked the Commission to consider potential impacts and accessibility
for homeowners at The CASE property adjacent to Malibu Bluffs Park as well as
restrictions on food trucks at the park.

In response to Commissioner Peak, Mr. Gold stated he had only seen three food
trucks on-site at the same time, but others had seen up to five food trucks.

Commissioner Peak stated there were no more than three food trucks on-site when
she had previously visited Malibu Bluffs Park on the weekends for local youth
sports organization games.

Commissioner Jenner indicated agreement with Commissioner Peak.

Jake Lingo stated staff should continue researching potential options that would
confo1m to the current zoning designation for Malibu Bluffs Park to avoid the need
to complete a zoning text amendment.

Robert Gold stated the zoning text amendment process was a complex process that
would take years to complete.

Community Services Deputy Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

Commissioner Guldimann requested Planning Department staff be present at the
November 15, 2022 Regular meeting to answer questions regarding the zoning
designation of Malibu Bluffs Park.

Commissioner Goldfarb stated she needed additional information before making a
recommendation regarding the Snack Shack project.

Commissioner Guldimann questioned the necessity of completing a zoning text
amendment due to the cost, staff time, and approval requirements.

Commissioner Peak stated the Commission should consider a long-term plan for
Malibu Bluffs Park and move forward with the zoning text amendment.
Commissioner Guldimann stated four zoning text amendments could be processed
each year. She stated if the Commission were to recommend one to City Council,
her preference would be for a zoning text amendment to change the zoning
designation for the Heathercliff property to allow a community center and pool.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of October 18, 2022
  Page 4 of6

  Chair Skophammer stated the City Council should determine which zoning text
  amendments to prioritize in the work plan.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated she was uncomfortable with recommending a
  zoning text amendment for Malibu Bluffs Park and would not support a motion.

  Commissioner Goldfarb indicated agreement with Commissioner Guldimann and
  requested Planning Department staff attend the November 15, 2022 Regular
  meeting to address zoning designation questions.

  Commissioner Peak stated food trucks were not a long-term solution to the issues
  surrounding the Snack Shack project. She stated food trucks do not always show as
  expected due to the long commute to Malibu.

MOTION  Chair Skophammer moved, and Vice Chair Jenner seconded a motion to
  recommend the City Council add the replacement of the Snack Shack with a like-
  for-like structure to the City Council Work Plan for Fiscal Year 2023-2024. The
  question was called, and the motion canied 3-1-1; Commissioner Goldfarb
  dissented, and Commissioner Guldimann abstained.

  B.  Parks and Recreation Master Plan
  Recommended Action: 1) Review and discuss the Parks and Recreation Master
  Plan; and 2) Provide a recommendation regarding the priority of facilities and
  amenities for City Council consideration.

  Community Services Director Bobbett presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated the Commission should recommend to City
  Council to rezone the property to build a community center and swimming pool
  with library services.

MOTION  Commissioner Guldimann moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion
  to recommend the City Council move forward with completing a zoning text
  amendment to the Heathercliff Property to allow a community center with library
  component and a swimming pool.

  Chair Skophammer stated he would like to discuss the item further before moving
  forward with the motion.

  Commissioner Peak stated the ideal location for a swimming pool would be the Ioki
  Property at Civic Center Way and Stuart Ranch Road.

  Commissioner Guldimann stated a swimming pool on the Ioki Property would not
  work due to waterboard issues and the property's slope.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of October 18, 2022
  Page 5 of 6

  Commissioner Peak expressed her concerns regarding traffic issues at the
  Heathercliff Property.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Chair Skophammer moved to recommend the City Council add the construction of
  a multigenerational recreation center with library services and a swimming pool
  utilizing Library set-aside funds on the Heathercliff Property to the City Council
  Work Plan for Fiscal Year 2023-2024. Commissioner Guldimann accepted the
  amendment.

  The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

ITEMS  NEW BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM6  STAFF UPDATES

  Community Services Deputy Director Riesgo provided an update on Charmlee
  Wilderness Park and Trancas Field.

  Recreation Manager Gallo provided an update on Tiny Tot Olympics and Senior
  Center programs.

  Community Services Director Bobbett provided an update on the Permanent Skate
  Park, pending Commission projects, and department staff changes.

ITEM7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Peak stated weekend visitors using the sports field at Malibu
  Elementary School did not have vehicle access to the parking lot and could only
  enter the field on foot through the parking lot gate. She stated the gate on Grayfox
  Street was locked.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Bobbett stated
  Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District was responsible for opening the gates
  at Malibu Elementary School and staff would follow up with them.

  Commissioner Peak expressed concerns regarding public safety at Malibu Bluffs
  Park and Legacy Park and inquired about a security guard or a park ranger.

  Commissioner Guldimann indicated agreement with Commissioner Peak. She
  stated she contacted Dr. Dana Graulich, owner of the Malibu Coast Animal
  Hospital, regarding public safety and recent vandalism.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of October 18, 2022
  Page 6 of 6

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Community Services Director Bobbett
  stated turf renovations at Malibu Bluffs Park occur twice a year. He stated heavy
  use by sports leagues and a limited renovation time period limits the success of the
  turf establishment. He stated staff would research cost-effective turf improvement
  options.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Park Security
  Malibu Bluffs Park Turf Improvements

  unanimously.

  Approved and adopted by the Parks and
  Recreation Commission of the City of
  Malibu on November 15, 2022.

Subject:  Community Services Department Monthly Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file a report of activities, events, projects, and
programs coordinated by the Community Services Department during October 2022.

DISCUSSION: The Community Services Department coordinated the following activities,
projects, and programs in October 2022.

RECREATION

Aquatics : Aquatics staff attended an in-service training on October 8. Training topics
included hypothermia, cardiac arrest signs and symptoms, and in-water rescue skills for
passive and active drowning.

Registration opened on October 26 for the Winter 2022-2023 Malibu Aquatics Foundation
Seawolves Swim Team and Masters Adult Conditioning Program . Thirty-four participants
registered for the program beginning on November 28.

Learn to Swim Lessons and Aqua Aerobics concluded on October 29 and will resume in
Spring 2023.

Community Classes: Dog Obedience with Canine Logic concluded on October 18. Ten
participants learned techniques to introduce their dogs to behaviors and socialization skills
through positive reinforcement.

Fall community classes continued through October, including adult barre fitness,
cartooning, chess, guitar, hip-hop dance, karate, musical theater, science, soccer, and t-
ball.

  Page 1 of 3  Agenda Item # 3.B.2.
 Seniors: Weekly Senior recreation programs offered in October include Art Trek, ballet,
cardio salsa, chair yoga, choir, knitting, mat yoga, Pilates, relax through coloring, stretch
and strength, tai chi, and tap dance.

The Senior Center temporarily closed from October 24 through November 11 for the
Regional Vote Center for the November 8, 2022, General Election. Senior Center classes
and programs were relocated to Malibu Bluffs Park. The Computer Lab remained open,
and staff assisted seniors with the Dial-A-Ride program and other Senior Services.

On October 12, John Mallett from Mainstreet Mortgage provided a free lecture on tools
and strategies for homeownership success.

A Halloween-themed luncheon for forty-eight participants took place on October 13.
Attendees were provided lunch from El Pollo Loco, and Micah the Magician performed at
the event. Key Home Care Services provided Halloween and Dfa de Los Muertos-themed
sugar cookies.

On October 26, participants attended an excursion to the Los Angeles Original Farmers
Market and the Grove. They enjoyed a tour of the Farmer's Market's food tastings and
shopping.

Social Media: Department social media featured community programs, Halloween events,
Malibu Arts programs, and Senior Center programs. Social media analytics indicate 1,575
followers, with 20% being Malibu residents.

Special Events: The Department hosted a Halloween-themed Park Tales, in partnership
with the Malibu Library, on October 13 at Malibu Bluffs Park. Fifteen families received a
goodie bag with City program flyers, snacks, and a book donated by the Malibu Library.

On October 28, over two hundred people attended the Halloween Bu-Bash Carnival at
Malibu Bluffs Park. Children aged nine and under enjoyed Halloween-themed carnival
games and activities. Event highlights included bounce houses, face painting, food trucks,
a costume catwalk, an art activity with the Malibu Library, and trunk-or-treat hosted by
Pepperdine Athletics. This was the first Halloween Carnival event since October 2019.

Sports: The Youth and Middle School Basketball Leagues for the Winter 2022-2023
season returned after a three-year break due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Middle School
Basketball player evaluations were held on October 26 at the Malibu High School Small
Gymnasium for forty-five participants. The Youth Basketball League for children in
kindergarten through fifth grade has seventy-one participants.

On October 2, Malibu Water Polo Foundation staff led a Girl's Water Polo Clinic at the
Malibu Community Pool. Seven participants learned fundamental water polo skills,
including passing, shooting, and defense. On October 16, nine girls attended the Girl's
Tennis Clinic, instructed by John Rom. The clinics were a part of the "Play Like a Girl
Malibu" program to encourage female sports participation.

  Page 2 of 3  Agenda Item# 3.B.2.
 PARK MAINTENANCE

Charmlee Wilderness Park: Trail crews continued working on the Ocean View Trail and
have built water bars and stairs to mitigate long-term erosion issues on steep trails.

Various upgrades and repairs were completed at the residence trailer, including new
flooring, duct cleaning, removal of flex ductwork, and installation of new ductwork.

Legacy Park: Removed graffiti from an electrical panel.

Pressure-washed all park statues, benches, drinking fountains, and hard surfaces.

Malibu Bluffs Park: Painted and covered graffiti in the men's exterior restroom.

Removed wind-damaged playground equipment and repaired the rubber surface.

Removed a faulty playground sand digger. A replacement bucket has been ordered and
will be installed upon delivery.

Removed graffiti and stickers from various locations throughout the skate park. Touch-up
paint was also applied to repaired structured areas.

Relocated a concrete memorial bench near the whale tail area.

Malibu City Hall: Pruned a tree in the upper parking lot.

Michael Landon Center: Installed new window blinds on office doors.

Purchased and installed new floor mats with the city logo.

Replaced a faulty toilet diaphragm in the women's exterior restroom.

Completed repairs on the locks located on the office door and men's exterior restroom.

Trancas Canyon Park: Replaced eight "No Parking Fire Lane" signs with updated signage.

Completed turf renovation and removed the temporary fencing around the Multipurpose
Field.

ATTACHMENTS: None.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Develop a list of the Commission's activities for the period of
July through December 2022 to be included in the City Manager's Mid-Year Commission
Activity Report, scheduled to be presented to the City Council at its Regular meeting on
February 13, 2023.

annual assignments for the Parks and Recreation Commission for Fiscal Year 2022-2023
(Attachment 1). The assignments include the requirement for each Commission to provide
the City Council with a mid-year written report of Commission activities.

The Commission is requested to develop a list of its activities during the first half of the
fiscal year, July through December 2022. The City Manager will present the mid-year

regarding the report.

Staff has prepared a draft report of the Commission's completed assignments since July
2022 (Attachment 2). The Commission is asked to review the Draft Mid-Year Report and
provide feedback.

SUBJECT:  Parks and Recreation Commission Mid-Year Activity Report

As directed by the City Council at its June 13, 2022 Regular meeting, the Parks and Recreation
Commission submits the following summary of its activities during the first half of Fiscal Year 2022-
2023 (July through December), approved at the Commission's Regular meeting on November 15,

  •  Reviewed and provided feedback regarding Community Services Department programs and

  •  Recommended two award recipients for the 2022 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award.

  •  Reviewed the Parks Master Plan and recommended Council consider adding an item to the

  •  Reviewed and evaluated options for the replacement of the Malibu Bluffs Park Snack Shack

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

ITEMS  NEW BUSINESS

  A.  Parks and Recreation Commission Mid-Year Activity Report
  Recommended Action: Develop a list of the Commission's activities for the period
  of July through December 2022 to be included in the City Manager's Mid-Year
  Commission Activity Report, scheduled to be presented to the City Council at its
  Regular meeting on February 13, 2023.

  Acting Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Acting Community Services Director
  Riesgo stated the removal of the invasive species at Trancas Field was conducted
  in Fiscal Year 2021-2022. She stated the Commission has reviewed and provided
  feedback regarding the removal of seedlings at Trancas Field in Fiscal Year 2022-
  2023.

  In response to Chair Skophammer, Commissioner Peak stated Recreation
  Supervisor Orosz was coordinating Earth Friendly Management Policy (EFMP)
  public education outreach with the Boys and Girls Club of Malibu.

  Chair Skophammer requested including EFMP public education outreach to the
  mid-year activity report.

  Commissioner Peak suggested a modification to include EFMP public education
  outreach focused on Malibu Elementary and Webster Elementary School.

  Commissioner Guldimann requested a Special meeting to tour the parks and vacant
  properties.

  In response to Acting Community Services Director Riesgo, Commissioner
  Guldimann stated the Special Meeting would include a tour of Las Flores Creek
  Park, Legacy Park, Malibu Bluffs Park, Ioki property, and the La Paz property. She
  stated the Commission could schedule a second Special meeting for the remaining
  parks.

  Commissioner Peak stated the Commission provided feedback regarding the
  rattlesnake precaution video and rattlesnake signage.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Acting Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated staff had not completed the emergency call boxes project.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Acting Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated several Pepperdine University athletes volunteered at Tiny Tot Olympics and
  Halloween Carnival in 2022. She stated Recreation Manager Gallo could contact
  Pepperdine University athletics department to potentially coordinate mentorship
  youth programs or clinics in 2023.

CONSENSUS By Consensus, the Commission approved the recommended Parks and Recreation
  Commission Mid-Year Activity Report with three additions 1) Reviewed and
  provided feedback regarding Trancas Field seedling removal, 2) Continued Earth
  Friendly Management Policy public education outreach focused on Malibu
  Elementary School and Webster Elementary School, and 3) Worked with staff to
  create a video on rattlesnake warnings and installed rattlesnake warning signs at
  City parks.
